Rashi on Ketubot 40b:10:1.hebrew: זו דברי ר"מ - דאמר אין קנס לקטנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:10:1.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir - Who says there is no fine for a minor [girl].

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:10:2.hebrew: מבת ג' שנים - שביאתה ביאה, ואין בתוליה חוזרין:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:10:2.english: From three years old - For intercourse with her is [legally considered] intercourse, and her hymen does not regenerate.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:11:1.english: Sale, no? - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:11:2.hebrew: אף קנס במקום מכר - משתהא ראויה לביאה עד שתביא שתי שערות, הוו תרוייהו; ומשהביאה שערות עד שתבגר, קנס ולא מכר:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:11:2.english: Even a fine where [she is subject to] sale - From when she is fit for intercourse until she grows two [pubic] hairs, both apply; and from when she has grown [two] hairs until she reaches majority, [there is a] fine, and not sale.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:11:3.hebrew: מאי טעמא דר"מ - דאמר קטנה אין לה קנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:11:3.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir - Who says [that] a minor girl has no fine.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:11:4.english: For the verse says - Regarding the fine, "and to him she shall be as a wife."

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:11:5.english: With regard to one who makes herself [a wife] - Scripture is speaking of one who has the capacity to give herself in marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:12:1.hebrew: אהא מתניתו לה - להא דריש לקיש, דאמר כ"מ שנכתב נער בלא ה' וקרינן נערה, ללמד על הקטנה בא:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:12:1.english: You teach it concerning that - [Referring] to that [statement] of Reish Lakish, who said [that] wherever na'ar is written without a heh and we read [it as] na'ara, it comes to teach regarding a minor girl.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:12:2.english: An evil name [i.e., slander] - [Saying:] "I did not find tokens of virginity in your daughter."

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:12:3.hebrew: פטור - ד"וענשו אותו מאה כסף ונתנו לאבי הנערה", מלא כתיב:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:12:3.english: Is exempt - For [in the verse,] "And they shall fine him one hundred [shekels of] silver and give [them] to the father of the young woman [na'ara]," [na'ara] is written in full.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:13:1.hebrew: אלא כאן נערה - האי דכתיב נערה מלא, לאו לגלויי עליה אתא אלא על כל מקום שנאמר נער חסר. ויליף הכי: כאן, שאי אפשר אלא בנערה, כתיב נערה מלא, וללמדך דכל מקום שנאמר נער — אפילו קטנה במשמע:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:13:1.english: Rather, here [it is] na'arah - That na'arah is written in full [with a heh] did not come to teach [something] about itself, but rather about every place where na'ar is stated defective [without a heh]. And it derives [it] thus: Here, where it is only possible [for the punishment to apply] to a na'arah, na'arah is written in full, to teach you that in any place where na'ar is stated — even a minor girl is included in the meaning.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:2:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבי זירא - מהכא מסתברא שאין בושת בכלל חמשים, דאם כן, אין הפרש בין בעל שלימה לבעל פגומה שנבעלה שלא כדרכה. והיכן הוא הפרש שביניהם? ש"מ גבי בושת, כיון שנפגמה כבר, אין בושתה רב כשלימה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:2:1.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said - From here it stands to reason that humiliation is not included in the fifty [sela], for if [it were] so, there is no difference between one who engaged in intercourse with an untainted [virgin] and one who engaged in intercourse with a tainted [virgin] who was penetrated unnaturally. And where is the difference between them? Learn from here [that it is] with respect to humiliation: since she has already been tainted, her humiliation is not as great as [that of] an untainted [virgin].

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:3:1.english: Because he tormented her - [This] is written regarding [the] fifty [shekels of] silver.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:3:2.hebrew: מכלל דבושת ופגם - שאינם משום עינוי, שהרי ישנן בשאר חובלין, אינו בכלל זה. פגם הוא נזק הנישום נמי בשאר חבלות:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:3:2.english: From which [it may be inferred] that humiliation and degradation - which are not on account of torment, since they apply in [the case of] other injurers, are not included in this [fine]. Degradation is [the] damage that is also appraised in [the case of] other injuries.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:4:1.hebrew: ואימא לדידה הוי - דבשלמא קנס, כתיב ביה "ונתן לאבי הנערה", אלא הני ליהוו לדידה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:4:1.english: And say it is hers - For granted, [regarding] the fine, it is written concerning it, "and he shall give to the father of the young woman"; however, let these [other payments] be hers.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:4:2.hebrew: בנעוריה בית אביה - גבי נדרים כתיב, ומיהו איכא למשמע מינה דבימי נעוריה תלאה הכתוב בבית אביה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:4:2.english: In her young womanhood, in her father's house - [This] is written regarding vows; nevertheless, one can infer from it that in the days of her young womanhood, Scripture attached her to her father's house.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:5:1.english: His daughter as a maidservant - [Scripture] juxtaposed a daughter to a maidservant.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:5:2.hebrew: תיפוק ליה כו' - אלא על כרחך, מהתם לא מצי למילף, דההוא בהפרת נדרים כתיב:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:5:2.english: Let him derive it, etc. - Rather, perforce, one cannot derive [it] from there, for that [verse] is written regarding the nullification of vows.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:6:1.hebrew: נילף מקנסא - מה קנסה לאביה, אף שאר שבח ממון נעורים לאביה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:6:1.english: Let us derive [it] from a fine - Just as her fine [goes] to her father, so too any other monetary profit of [her] youth [goes] to her father.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:6:2.hebrew: אלא מסתברא - דבושת ופגם דאב הויא, שהרי בידו לביישה בבושת בעילה ולפוגמה בפגם בעילה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:6:2.english: Rather, it is reasonable - that [the payments for] humiliation and degradation belong to the father, since it is within his power to humiliate her with the humiliation of intercourse and to degrade her with the degradation of intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:6:3.english: For if he wished, he could hand her over - to betroth her through intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:6:4.hebrew: למנוול ומוכה שחין - כדתנן לקמן: "האב זכאי בבתו בקידושי', בכסף ובשטר ובביאה". וכיון דבידו ליטול ממון לפוגמה ולביישה בושה זו, השתא אפסדיה האי דפגמה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:6:4.english: To a repulsive [man] or one afflicted with boils - As we learned in the Mishnah later: "A father has authority over his daughter regarding her betrothal — [effected] through money, through a document, or through intercourse." And since it is in his power to take money to degrade her and to humiliate her with this humiliation, now this [man] who degraded her has caused him [the father] a loss.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:8:1.hebrew: [מאי נפקא ליה - לכל אדם בבעילתה, אם בעולה היא, הואיל ולמלאכה קיימא]:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:8:1.english: What difference is there to him - to any person regarding her [prior] intercourse, whether she is a non-virgin, since she is [designated] for work?

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:8:2.hebrew: ולעבדו מאי נפקא ליה - למריה מינה? אם בעולה היא, מי קפיד מריה? אלא שיהו להן ולדות:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:8:2.english: And to his slave, what difference is there to him - [meaning,] to his master, from her? If she is a non-virgin, does his master care? [All he cares is] that they have offspring.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:8:3.hebrew: קורת רוח - שזהיר בעבודתו, ואף הוא רוצה לעשות לו נחת רוח להטעימו טעם בתולה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:8:3.english: Satisfaction - That [the slave] is diligent in his work, and he [the master] also wants to give him satisfaction, to let him experience the taste of a virgin.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:9:1.hebrew: כ"מ שיש מכר - לאב בבתו, דהיינו בקטנותה:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:9:1.english: Any place where there is sale - for a father [to sell] his daughter, which is during her minority.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:9:2.english: He [the father] has no fine for her - For there is no fine for a minor.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:9:3.english: Any place where there is a fine - From when she is a young woman.

Rashi on Ketubot 40b:9:4.hebrew: אין מכר - דתניא (ערכין דף כט:): יכול ימכור אדם בתו כשהיא נערה? אמרת: מכורה כבר יוצאה. עכשיו שאינה מכורה, אינו דין שלא תימכר:
Rashi on Ketubot 40b:9:4.english: There is no sale - As it was taught [in a baraita] (Arachin 29b): Could [it be that] a person may sell his daughter when she is a young woman? You say: [If she was] already sold, she goes free; now that she is not sold, is it not logical that she cannot be sold?

Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:13:1.hebrew: הא לאו הכי ה"א אפילו קטנה, והכתיב אם אמת היה וכו' - תימה לר"י: מה בכך אם קרא איירי בבת עונשין? מ"מ מצינו למימר דה"ה קטנה, דהא בא על קטנה מאורסה הוי בסקילה לרבנן בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף סו:), אע"ג דההיא פרשה דנערה המאורסה בבת עונשין כתיבא [כדכתיב: "ואת הנערה על דבר אשר לא צעקה"]. ותירץ: דהתם משום דמסקינן בסמוך: "כאן 'נערה', הא כל מקום שנאמר 'נער' אפילו קטנה במשמע", הלכך מחייבין ליה התם, וכולהו עריות ילפי מינה. אי נמי: דוקא במוציא שם רע סברא הוא לומר דלא מחייב קנס ומלקות אלא בגדולה כיון דקרא איירי בבת עונשין, ולא בעלמא — משום דמוציא שם רע על הקטנה סברא הוא דפטור, דפיתוי קטנה אונס הוא, והוי כמוציא שם רע על הנערה שנאנסה דלא מחייב. אבל אין לומר דמסתבר ליה דדוקא בבת עונשין מחייב ליה משום שבא להורגה, דבפרק קמא דסנהדרין (דף ח:), בשמעתא דחוששין ללעז, משמע דלאו משום דקא גריס לה קטלא מיחייב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:13:1.english: "If that were not the case, I would have said [that it applies] even [to] a minor! But isn't it written: 'And if [this matter] was true,' etc." - The Ri is perplexed: What difference does it make if the verse is speaking of one who is subject to punishment? Nevertheless, we could say that the same law applies to a minor, for one who has intercourse with a betrothed minor is [liable] to stoning according to the Rabbis in chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 66b), even though that passage of a betrothed na'ara is written regarding one who is subject to punishment [as it is written: "and the na'ara because she did not cry out"]. And he answered: There, it is because we conclude immediately below: "Here [it is written] na'ara, which implies that any place where na'ar is stated, even a minor is indicated"; therefore, we hold him liable there, and all [other] forbidden sexual relations are derived from it. Alternatively, specifically in the case of a slanderer, it is logical to say that he is liable for the fine and lashes only for an adult [na'ara] since the verse is speaking of one who is subject to punishment, and not elsewhere — because [regarding] one who slanders a minor, it is logical that he is exempt, since the seduction of a minor is [considered] rape, and it is like one who slanders a na'ara who was raped, where he is not liable. However, one cannot say that it seems logical to him that he is liable specifically with one who is subject to punishment because he comes to have her killed; for in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (8b), in the discussion of "we are concerned about disrepute," it is implied that he is not liable because he causes her death.

Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:2:1.hebrew: אחד כדרכה ואחד שלא כדרכה - שלא כדרכה ה"ל למינקט ברישא; אלא כן דרך הש"ס שאינו חושש, כדנקט לעיל (כתובות דף לה.) בתנא דבי חזקיה: "בין מתכוין לשאין מתכוין", דה"ל למינקט "שאין מתכוין" ברישא כדקתני "בין שוגג למזיד" — אלא כן דרך הש"ס במקום שצריך לשנות הן ולאו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:2:1.english: One vaginal intercourse, and one anal intercourse - It should have stated "anal intercourse" first; however, such is the style of the Talmud that it is not particular [about the order], just as it stated earlier (Ketubot 35a) in [the baraita of] the school of Chizkiyah: "whether intentional or unintentional," where it should have stated "unintentional" first, just as it teaches "whether unwitting or deliberate" — rather, such is the style of the Talmud in a place where it needs to teach "yes" and "no" [i.e., a positive and negative pair].

Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:2:2.hebrew: יאמרו בעל שלימה חמשים - פירוש: הראשון שבא עליה שלא כדרכה, דמחייב קנס אפילו שלא כדרכה, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקידושין (דף ט:): "באו עליה י' ועדיין היא בתולה כו'", פירוש — שלא כדרכה, וקאמר: "מודה רבי לענין קנס דכולהו משלמי". ובפרק הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נט. ושם), גבי "ולו תהיה לאשה" — באשה הראויה לו, פרט לאלמנה לכ"ג כו', ופריך: היכי דמי? אילימא כדרכה, תיפוק ליה דהויא לה בעולה! אלא לאו שלא כדרכה. והכא הוה מצי למינקט שבאו עליה ב' שלא כדרכה. וכן בפרק בן סורר (סנהדרין עג:), דמוקי ההיא דאלו נערות שיש להן קנס כגון שבא עליה שלא כדרכה וחזר ובא עליה כדרכה — הוה מצי למינקט "וחזר ובא עליה שלא כדרכה". ומה שקשה על פירוש הקונטרס דהתם — פירשנו בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נט.) ובפרק קמא דקידושין (דף ט:):
Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:2:2.english: "They will say: [one who] had intercourse with an untainted [virgin pays] fifty" - Explanation: the first one had anal intercourse with her, for one is liable for the fine even for anal intercourse, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (9b): "Ten [men] had intercourse with her and she is still a virgin, etc." — meaning, anal intercourse — and it states: "Rabbi concedes regarding the fine that all of them pay." And in the chapter Haba al Yevimto (Yevamot 59a and there), regarding [the verse] "and she shall be his wife" — [teaching that it refers to] a woman who is fit for him, excluding a widow to a High Priest, etc. — [the Gemara] asks: What is the case? If we say [he had] vaginal intercourse [with her], let it derive from the fact that she has become a non-virgin! Rather, is it not [a case of] anal intercourse? And here [in our Gemara, Rabbi Zeira] could have taken [a case] where two [men] had anal intercourse with her. Similarly, in the chapter Ben Sorer (Sanhedrin 73b), where [the Gemara] establishes that [Mishnah] in Elu Ne'arot [teaching] that they receive a fine as a case where he had anal intercourse with her and then had vaginal intercourse with her, it could have taken [the case of] "and then had anal intercourse with her." And as for what is difficult with the explanation of Rashi there, we have already explained [it] in Haba al Yevimto (Yevamot 59a) and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (9b).

Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:4:1.hebrew: ואימא לדידה - אע"ג דפרישית לעיל (כתובות דף לח:) דבושת ופגם הוקשו לקנס, וניתן למי שקנס ניתן — היינו בתר דקים לן הכא דהוי הכל לאביה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:4:1.english: "And say [that they go] to her" - Even though I explained earlier (Ketubot 38b) that [payments for] embarrassment and blemish were compared to the fine, and are given to the one to whom the fine is given — that is [only] after we have established here that everything belongs to her father.

Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:6:1.hebrew: מסתברא דאביה הוי דאי בעי כו' - וא"ת: אמאי לא קאמר דאביה הוי מדקא יהיב מפתה, כדאמר לקמן בריש נערה (כתובות דף מב.)? וי"ל: דלמא לא יהיב מפתה, דקראי דאביי ורבא באונס כתיבי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:6:1.english: It is reasonable that it belongs to her father, as if he wished, etc. - And if you ask: Why does [the Gemara] not say that it belongs to her father from [the fact] that a seducer pays [these], as it says later at the beginning of [the chapter] Na'arah (Ketubot 42a)? One can answer that perhaps a seducer does not pay [these], for the verses [cited by] Abaye and Rava are written regarding a rapist.

Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:6:2.hebrew: דאי בעי מסר לה למנוול ומוכה שחין - וממעשה ידיה ליכא למילף, דהא מיתזנא מיניה, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא דקדושין (דף ד. ושם); ולא מקדושין, דמעלמא קאתו לה; ומתרוייהו נמי לא, דחבלה דגופה שאני. תימה, דהכא לא קים לן בושת ופגם דהוי לאביה אלא מכח שיכול לקדשה למנוול ומוכה שחין, ואם כן היכי בעי למימר בריש קדושין (דף ג:) גבי קדושי כסף, מנא לן דמיקדשה בכסף וקידושין דאביה הן: "וכי תימא נילף מבושת ופגם"? הא בושת ופגם גופיה לא קים לן אלא מכח שיכול לקדשה! ואומר ר"י, דאורחיה דהש"ס דבעי לדחויי, אפילו קים לן דבושת ופגם הוי דאביה ממקום אחר. א"נ, התם בעי למילף קדושי נערה מבושת ופגם של קטנה, ומקדושי קטנה הוה יליף להו אי לאו דהוה אמינא הני מילי קטנה דלית לה יד, ונערה אית לה יד, כדאמרינן התם לעיל; ולהכי קאמר: "וכי תימא נילף מבושת ופגם דקטנה", אע"ג דלהכי אית לה יד — כדאמרינן בהחובל (ב"ק דף פז:): "יעשה לה סגולה" — ואפ"ה הוי דאביה, ה"נ קדושי נערה. ואם היינו מפרשים דלא קאי אקדושין הא דקאמר "ונילף מבושת ופגם", אלא אמעשה ידיה דאייתי התם לעיל — הוה אתי שפיר, אבל לא משמע הכי; ועוד, דא"כ הכא נמי ה"ל לאסוקי: "וכ"ת נילף מבושת ופגם", כיון דאמעשה ידיה קאי, וכן לקמן בפרק נערה (כתובות דף מו:):
Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:6:2.english: "As if he wished he could give her [in marriage] to a repulsive [man] or one afflicted with boils" - And from her handiwork one cannot derive [that humiliation and degradation belong to her father], because she is sustained by him, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (4a and there); nor from [her] betrothal [money], because it comes to her from elsewhere; and from both of them [together] also not, because injury to her body is different. This is puzzling, for here we do not know that humiliation and degradation belong to her father except by virtue of [the fact] that he can betroth her to a repulsive [man] or one afflicted with boils; and if so, how could [the Gemara] seek to say at the beginning of Kiddushin (3b) regarding betrothal with money — [when asking] from where do we [know] that she is betrothed with money and that the betrothal [money] belongs to her father: "And if you say: Let us derive [it] from humiliation and degradation"? Why, humiliation and degradation itself we only know [belongs to her father] by virtue of [the fact] that he can betroth her! And R. Yitzchak says that it is the way of the Talmud that it wants to reject [the suggestion], even [granting that] we knew that humiliation and degradation belong to her father from another source. Alternatively, there it seeks to derive the betrothal [money] of a na'arah from the humiliation and degradation of a minor, and from the betrothal of a minor it would have derived it were it not that I would say: this applies only to a minor, who has no legal agency, whereas a na'arah has legal agency, as we say there earlier; and therefore it says: "And if you say: Let us derive [it] from the humiliation and degradation of a minor," even though in this respect she has legal agency — as we say in [chapter] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 87b): "a fund shall be made for her" — and nevertheless it belongs to her father; so too [with] the betrothal [money] of a na'arah. And if we were to explain that that which [the Gemara] says, "And let us derive [it] from humiliation and degradation," does not refer to betrothal [money], but rather to her handiwork which it brought there earlier — it would work out well, but it does not sound like that; and furthermore, if so, here too it should have raised [the question]: "And if you say: Let us derive [it] from humiliation and degradation," since it refers to her handiwork, and similarly later in chapter Na'arah (Ketubot 46b):

Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:7:1.hebrew: כמה אדם רוצה ליתן כו' להשיא לעבדו - תימה, דמה שומא היא זו? וכי אשה חשובה ממשפחה גדולה אינה נפסדת בפגמה אלא שוה שפחה הניסת לעבד? וי"ל, דכל אשה שמין לפי מה שהיא; בענין זה: כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בין בתולה לבעולה להשיא לעבדו אשה כזאת הנפגמת. והא דנקט שפחה — אורחא דמלתא נקט, דאין דרך להשיא לעבדו בת מלכים:
Tosafot on Ketubot 40b:7:1.english: How much a person is willing to give, etc., to marry [her] to his slave - [This is] astonishing! For what kind of assessment is this? Is a distinguished woman from a prominent family diminished in her degradation only [by] the value of a maidservant who is married to a slave? And one can say that every woman is assessed according to who she is, in this manner: how much a person is willing to give [as the difference] between a virgin and a non-virgin to marry off to his slave a woman such as this one who was degraded. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] mentioned "a maidservant," it stated the ordinary case, for it is not customary to marry off a princess to one's slave.
